title: The Transcendental Reals are an Explicit Dense Gδ
description: Strengthens the parent's 'transcendentals are residual' to the explicit structural statement that the transcendental reals {x : ℝ | ¬ IsAlgebraic ℚ x} are themselves a concrete dense Gδ set — the named residual witness requested by the parent's open question. Proves the abstract lemma that in any T1 space the complement of a countable set is a Gδ (a countable intersection of open singleton-complements), and that in a perfect T1 Baire space it is moreover dense. As a dual corollary it establishes the analogue of 'ℚ is not a Gδ': the algebraic reals, being dense yet meagre, are not a Gδ set.

overview.historicalContext: The Baire category theorem (René-Louis Baire, 1899) divides subsets of a complete metric space into meagre (first category, topologically negligible) and residual (comeagre) classes, with a Gδ — a countable intersection of open sets — as the canonical 'large' shape. A classical exercise, recorded in Oxtoby's Measure and Category (GTM 2, 1971), shows the irrationals are a dense Gδ while ℚ, being a dense countable Fσ, is not a Gδ. Cantor's 1874 countability of the algebraic numbers and Liouville's 1844 construction of transcendentals make {x : ℝ | IsAlgebraic ℚ x} a countable set, so the algebraic/transcendental split is the exact algebraic analogue of the rational/irrational one: the transcendentals are residual and dense. The parent entry 'The Algebraic Reals are Meagre' proves that residuality; this entry upgrades the abstract 'residual' membership to a concrete dense Gδ witness, mirroring Mathlib's IsGδ.setOf_irrational and dense_irrational for the irrationals.
overview.problemStatement:
Exhibit the transcendental reals $\{x : \mathbb{R} \mid 
eg\,\mathrm{IsAlgebraic}\;\mathbb{Q}\;x\}$ as an explicit dense $G_\delta$ set in $\mathbb{R}$ — the concrete residual witness the parent's open question requests, strictly stronger than mere membership in the residual filter. Concretely: prove $\mathrm{IsG}_\delta\,\{x \mid 
eg\,\mathrm{IsAlgebraic}\;\mathbb{Q}\;x\} \wedge \mathrm{Dense}\,\{x \mid 
eg\,\mathrm{IsAlgebraic}\;\mathbb{Q}\;x\}$, abstracted to its natural generality (in any $T_1$ space the complement of a countable set is a $G_\delta$; in a perfect $T_1$ Baire space it is moreover dense). As a dual corollary, prove the algebraic reals $\{x \mid \mathrm{IsAlgebraic}\;\mathbb{Q}\;x\}$ are NOT a $G_\delta$ — the algebraic analogue of 'ℚ is not a Gδ'.
overview.proofStrategy: Write the algebraic reals as a countable set $A$; then the transcendentals are exactly $\bigcap_{a \in A} \{a\}^{c}$. The abstract lemma isGδ_compl_of_countable proves this is a Gδ in any T1 space: each singleton $\{a\}$ is closed (T1), so each $\{a\}^{c}$ is open, and the biInter over the countable index $A$ is a Gδ via IsGδ.biInter_of_isOpen. Density comes from dense_compl_of_countable: the countable set is meagre (reusing the parent's countable_isMeagre), and the complement of a meagre set is residual hence dense (dense_of_mem_residual). Combining gives the headline transcendentalReals_dense_isGδ; residuality is then re-derived directly from the dense Gδ via residual_of_dense_Gδ. The dual not_isGδ_of_dense_isMeagre argues by contradiction: if a dense meagre set $s$ were a Gδ it would be residual, forcing $s^{c}$ meagre too, so $s \cup s^{c} = \mathrm{univ}$ would be meagre — impossible in a nonempty Baire space (not_isMeagre_of_isOpen). Instantiating at the algebraic reals (dense because they contain the dense ℚ via isAlgebraic_rat and Rat.denseRange_cast, meagre by the parent) yields algebraicReals_not_isGδ. All six results close with #print axioms confirming 0 axioms beyond the standard Mathlib triple.
keyInsights: Being a dense Gδ is strictly stronger than being residual: 'residual' is by definition only membership in the filter generated by dense Gδ sets, so it asserts a set contains a dense Gδ without naming one. Here the transcendentals are exhibited as one — the concrete witness, not just the abstract membership.

The whole construction is a single set identity: {x | ¬ IsAlgebraic ℚ x} = ⋂_{a algebraic} {a}ᶜ. The Gδ structure is then automatic from T1 (singletons closed ⟹ complements open) plus countability of the index set; no analysis of transcendence is needed beyond countability.

The right level of generality is purely topological: T1 alone gives 'countable complement is a Gδ', and adding perfect + Baire gives density. This decouples the result from ℝ-specific facts and reuses verbatim for any countable set in a suitable space, exactly as Mathlib treats the irrationals.

'Not a Gδ' has a clean abstract mechanism (not_isGδ_of_dense_isMeagre): a dense Gδ is residual, so if a dense meagre set were a Gδ, both it and its complement would be meagre, making the whole space meagre — contradicting the Baire property. Density and meagreness are jointly incompatible with the Gδ shape.

The pairing is a perfect dichotomy: the transcendentals are a dense Gδ, while the algebraic reals are dense (they contain ℚ) yet meagre and therefore not a Gδ — the algebraic/transcendental analogue of the classical irrational/rational Gδ/Fσ contrast.

The abstract lemma isGδ_compl_of_countable coincides with Mathlib's existing Set.Countable.isGδ_compl but is re-proved in-file from IsGδ.biInter_of_isOpen; the genuinely new content is the concrete transcendental dense-Gδ result and the algebraic-reals not-Gδ corollary, for which Mathlib supplies only the irrational/rational analogue.

conclusion.summary: A 165-line, 0-sorry, 0-axiom formalization exhibiting the transcendental reals as an explicit dense Gδ set in ℝ — the concrete residual witness requested by the parent's open question — built on a reusable abstract lemma that the complement of a countable set is a Gδ in any T1 space (and a dense Gδ in a perfect T1 Baire space). A dual corollary proves the algebraic reals are not a Gδ, the analogue of the classical fact that ℚ is not a Gδ.
conclusion.implications: Being a dense Gδ is a strict topological strengthening of being residual: residual asserts only that a set contains a dense Gδ, whereas here the transcendentals are exhibited as one. The pairing transcendentals = dense Gδ versus algebraic reals = dense Fσ that is not Gδ is the exact analogue of irrationals/rationals, placing the algebraic-transcendental dichotomy alongside Mathlib's irrational/rational one. The abstract lemmas isGδ_compl_of_countable and not_isGδ_of_dense_isMeagre are reusable for any countable / dense-meagre set in suitable spaces.
openQuestions: Dualize to the algebraic reals as an explicit Fσ (countable union of closed singletons) and record the full Gδ/Fσ classification of the dichotomy.
Quantify the dense Gδ further: exhibit an explicit decreasing sequence of dense open sets whose intersection is the transcendentals, making the Gδ presentation fully constructive.
